Group.description:
What a computer offers, as one flat list: capabilities().groups, repeated in hello.groups. A sub-flag such as
input.touch is its own entry. Each is optional unless kind makes it Core. cdp, stream and downloads are the
provider's, not computerd's: cdp a browser's CDP target (ComputerConnection.cdp), stream a live view of the screen
(provider.stream()), downloads the files a browser saved; a daemon's hello never lists them.
Group.title: Group

MountSyncResult.description:
mount.sync: asks the computer's resident Archil sync server (its socket, ARCHIL_SYNC_SOCKET) for one sync of
/workspace, coalesced with any in flight, and answers its exit code: 0 is every write so far durable. A computer with
no Archil mount has no server: not_found.
MountSyncResult.title: MountSyncResult

exitCode.description: null while running, or when a signal ended it.
exitCode.title: exitCode

signal.description: The signal that ended it, without SIG: "TERM", "KILL".

argvClipped.description: argv was cut to its first arguments to keep the listing small.
argvClipped.title: argvClipped

exitCode.description: null while running, or when a signal ended it.
exitCode.title: exitCode

signal.description: The signal that ended it, without SIG: "TERM", "KILL".
signal.title: signal

from.description: Where the page starts: the page before's next, or 0 (the default) for the first page.
from.title: from

truncated.description: More follow: list again with from: next.
truncated.title: truncated

next.description: Where the page after this one starts. A process dropped from the table between pages moves no other past it.
next.title: next

stream.description: "stdout" or "stderr"; "pty" for a process started with one; "log" for one started with a log.
stream.title: stream

offset.description: Bytes since the process started. Pass the last read's nextOffset.
offset.title: offset

maxBytes.description: Default and most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES; more is refused as `limit`.
maxBytes.title: maxBytes

waitMs.description: When nothing past offset is there yet, wait up to this long (most MAX_READ_WAIT_MS) for bytes or the end.
waitMs.title: waitMs

dropped.description:
Bytes before offset the ring no longer held: the read began at the ring's start instead. Once an ended process's
ring is let go, every byte from offset on.
dropped.title: dropped

exited.description: The process has ended and nothing is left past nextOffset.
exited.title: exited

size.description: The stream's bytes so far: every byte since the process started, kept in the ring or dropped. For "log", the log's.
size.title: size

capped.description: "log" only: output came past the log's PROCESS_LOG_BYTES and was not written to it.
capped.title: capped

logError.description:
"log" only: a write to the log failed or wrote short (a full disk), so the log stopped there for good and holds
only the output before it: why. Nothing after it is written, so the file stays a true prefix.
logError.title: logError

signal.description:
INT to a process started with a pty is ^C: it goes to the terminal's foreground process group (the job a shell
runs in the foreground, or the program when it runs none), and is refused as denied when that group is outside
the program's session. Every other signal, and INT without a pty, goes to the program's process group. A signal
to a process that has ended does nothing.
signal.title: signal

note.description:
Set only for INT on a terminal: when it found no foreground group (the program let go of it, or is ending) and went
to the program's own group, or when the foreground group had no process left in the program's session by the time
the guard came to signal it (it ended, and its id may have gone to a group in another session) and INT was not
sent: why.
note.title: note

argv.description: The program and its arguments, never a shell string.
argv.title: argv

env.description: Added over the same minimal default as exec.run's.
env.title: env

pty.description: Run in a terminal of this size: one "pty" stream, and the program's own session with it as the controlling terminal.
pty.title: pty

stdin.description: Keep stdin open for process.write. Without it (and without a pty), stdin is /dev/null.
stdin.title: stdin

log.description:
An absolute path for a new file the daemon writes the first PROCESS_LOG_BYTES of the output to, stdout and stderr
(or the terminal's) as they come, and read as the "log" stream. The daemon makes the missing directories and the
file itself (mode 0644, its own); a link at the path or at any directory on its way is refused as `denied`, a
file already there as `exists`, and nothing is started.
log.title: log

waitGroup.description:
The process runs until its program and every process left in its process group (with a pty, its session) have
ended, and reports the program's own exit. A signal goes to what is left of the group once the program is gone.
waitGroup.title: waitGroup

orphans.description: "keep": when the process ends, what it started outside it runs on, to the computer's end, instead of being ended.
orphans.title: orphans

id.description: The daemon's name for the process, such as "p1".
id.title: id

pid.description: The program's pid in the computer.
pid.title: pid

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the end, up to a day; 0 asks without waiting. On timeout, running is true.
timeoutMs.title: timeoutMs

data.description: base64, to stdin or the terminal.
data.title: data

close.description: Close stdin after the data. A terminal has no stdin to close: send "\x04" or signal HUP.
close.title: close

ScreenReadParams.description: One shot is held; it is dropped at eof or at the next shot.
ScreenReadParams.title: ScreenReadParams

region.description: Only this part of the screen; its coordinates stay those of the full screenshot.
region.title: region

size.description:
The PNG's bytes; data holds at most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES of it. The PNG is 8-bit and non-interlaced (gray, RGB, palette,
gray and alpha, or RGBA), as the conformance suite decodes it.
size.title: size

data.description: base64; read the rest with screen.read.
data.title: data

width.description: The image's pixels: the input coordinate space (never downscaled).
width.title: width

scale.description: Device pixels per logical point: 1 on Xvfb; a phone reports its own.
scale.title: scale

cursor.description: Where the pointer is, with input.pointer.
cursor.title: cursor

ScreenWatchParams.description:
The live view's frames (screen.watch): the next frame after the caller's ack, once the screen changed. `after` is
the seq of the last frame the caller has whole, 0 for none; an older one gets the newest frame at once.
ScreenWatchParams.title: ScreenWatchParams

waitMs.description: The longest wait for a change, in ms, 0 to 10000; default 2000.
waitMs.title: waitMs

maxWidth.description: The frame's width at most (scaled down, never up); default 1280.
maxWidth.title: maxWidth

ScreenWatchResult.description:
changed false: no change within waitMs, and no frame. A frame carries its bytes as screen.shot carries its PNG: the
first MAX_CHUNK_BYTES in data, the rest through screen.read by id.
ScreenWatchResult.title: ScreenWatchResult

format.description: jpeg from computerd; png from a phone client that encodes its own frames.
format.title: format

width.description: The screen's pixels: the input coordinate space.
width.title: width

cursor.description: Pixels of the full screenshot, origin top left. A region shot never changes this space.
cursor.title: cursor

path.description: A file (one entry, its name) or a directory (entries relative to it).
path.title: path

id.description: Ending a pull that is not open is fine.
id.title: id

maxBytes.description: Default and most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES; more is refused as `limit`.
maxBytes.title: maxBytes

data.description: base64: maxBytes of the archive, fewer only at its end.
data.title: data

path.description: The directory to extract into; made, with its parents, when missing.
path.title: path

data.description: base64. Send the next write after this one's reply: writes are extracted in the order they arrive.
data.title: data

bounds.title: bounds
